response.consequence: After a successful save, or any refetch that returns changed data, the event type editor unmounts and remounts. In-progress form state is lost, the UI flickers, and extra refetches are triggered.
response.explanation: The effect cleanup invalidates and resets the event-type query. This cleanup was meant to run only on unmount or when the id changed. The change adds `eventTypeQueryData` to the dependency array, so the cleanup now also runs every time the cached data changes. Examples are a refetch that returns different data after a save invalidates the query, or a window-focus refetch. When that happens, the cleanup from the previous render closes over truthy data and calls `resetQueries`. That clears the data, so `if (!eventTypeQueryData) return null` unmounts the whole EventType form. The form then remounts after a refetch.
response.title: Adding eventTypeQueryData to effect deps resets the query and unmounts the form whenever data changes

response.consequence: Users can no longer use "check for recordings" on past Cal Video bookings that have no recording yet. Recordings that exist but are not yet marked isRecorded cannot be fetched from the booking list.
response.explanation: The old code enabled the recordings button for past, confirmed Cal Video bookings that were not yet recorded. It labelled the button "check_for_recordings" so the user could fetch recordings. The refactor adds `(action.id === "view_recordings" && !booking.isRecorded)` to `disabled` in BookingListItem. getVideoOptionsActions in bookingActions.ts also sets `disabled: !(... && booking.isRecorded)` and uses the plain "view_recordings" label. For a past, confirmed Cal Video booking with isRecorded=false, the action is now always disabled, so the dialog that checks for recordings can never be opened. The old behavior of showing recordings for any recorded booking regardless of location is also changed: with isCalVideoLocation now required, recorded bookings at other locations are disabled.

other_findings.consequence: Organizers can confirm pending bookings that are unpaid but have the payment app enabled. The old code blocked this.
other_findings.explanation: The old condition was `(isPending && !paymentAppData.enabled) || (paymentAppData.enabled && !!price && booking.paid)`. It is now `(isPending && !showPendingPayment) || (showPendingPayment && booking.paid)`, where `showPendingPayment = enabled && payment.length && !paid`. The second clause can never be true, because showPendingPayment requires !paid. A pending booking with the payment app enabled, no payment rows and paid=false makes showPendingPayment falsy, so Confirm is shown. The old code hid Confirm in that case.
other_findings.title: showPendingPayment makes the confirm-action payment gating wrong

hypotheses.evidence_needed: Read the first part of toggleResourcePermissionLevel in usePermissions.ts (lines 66-80) to see whether `*.*` is removed before the per-resource branch. Then trace toggling a resource to "none" starting from ["*.*", ...all permissions], and check whether the result still contains `*.*`. Confirm or refute with the usePermissions tests, or add a toggle test.
hypotheses.failure_mode: When a role holds the wildcard `*.*` and an admin lowers one resource to "none" or "read", the `*.*` entry may not be removed. The new list could then still contain `*.*`, and the permission level would read back as "all". The role would keep full access when the admin meant to restrict it. The per-resource branch filters only entries starting with `${resource}.`, which doesn't match `*.*`. The `*.*` removal for non-wildcard resources may therefore be missing. The `hasAllPermissions` re-add check could also wrongly restore `*.*`.
hypotheses.investigation_rationale: This is the permission-editing logic for organization roles, so a wrong result changes what a role is allowed to do. The visible per-resource branch (lines 76-115) never strips `*.*`. The earlier lines in that function (the start of toggleResourcePermissionLevel, after line 69) were not shown, so I'm assuming `*.*` is handled there.
hypotheses.priority_rationale: A bug here would silently grant privileges that persist in the saved role. The new unit tests cover only getResourcePermissionLevel, not the toggle path.
